notes: How the values were read. The archive.org copy of the 1999 report (item DTIC_ADA366414, 351 leaves) serves per-page OCR as DjVu XML through its BookReader text endpoint; p. 8-5 is leaf 184 and p. 8-4 is leaf 183 (viewer: https://archive.org/details/DTIC_ADA366414/page/n184). Page 8-5 is a landscape table scanned sideways, so the rows were rebuilt from the word coordinates: each object class is a vertical strip and the columns are, in the report's own order (p. 8-4), Levels 1-4, slope (%), Y-intercept (cm/s), divergence angle (deg), standard error Sy/x (cm/s), reference notes; p. 8-4 gives the formula leeway speed (cm/s) = slope (%) x W10m (m/s) + Y-intercept (cm/s) and the worked example of slope 1.1 with intercept 3.5 giving 14.5 cm/s at 10 m/s. About a third of the p. 8-5 cells are garbled, and several digits were read upside down ('9T' for 1.6, '60' for 0.9, '601' for 109). Independent check: the Coast Guard's own 2005 report (Allen, Leeway Divergence, CG-D-05-05, archive.org item DTIC_ADA435435, 128 leaves) reproduces the PIW and Survival Craft part of Table 8-1 as Table 1-2 on p. 1-8 (leaf 23, a portrait page with clean OCR) and lists all 63 divergence angles in Table 1-3 (pp. 1-10 to 1-11). Wherever both OCRs are legible they agree (about 50 cells), and every Table 1-3 angle matches Table 8-1 where legible, so each row's note says which OCR each cell came from. One cell stays unread: the Y-intercept for 'no ballast, no canopy, no drogue' (both OCRs lose the decimal point; the digits are 1-0-9). Rows that rest on a single OCR reading are flagged in their notes. What is missing, hence 'partial': the Table 8-1 slope and intercept for the sea kayak, surfboard and skiffs (continuation pages 8-6 onward have no text layer) and sub-table 8-1A (deep-ballast 4-6 person rafts by drogue and loading); for those classes only the divergence angle is recorded, from the 2005 reproduction, and the rows say so. The 2005 report itself replaces slope-plus-angle with downwind and crosswind components (Tables 3-1, 3-2; 25 categories measured, 38 estimated); those are a different model and were not transcribed. Grades: A, as the Coast Guard R&D Center's own recommended values; rows read only from the 2005 reproduction are still the same organisation and author. Year is 1999 on every row because the values are the 1999 recommendations, even where the 2005 print was the legible copy. The correction to leeway-definition only updates its note, which says the values are not yet transcribed; the checker will warn that the task did not name that row. hf-radar-search-area: nothing opened here bears on it. Quotes kept to 12 words or fewer. Capsized here is a raft class name, not a distress report. The checker's 'equals A + B' warnings are arithmetic coincidences among 23 small one-decimal coefficients (for example 1.2 = 0.7 + 0.5): every value is a single printed cell of Table 8-1 or Table 1-3, nothing was summed, and the only way to silence them would be to drop rows. VERIFICATION 21 Oct 2026: all 23 rows confirmed on the archive.org per-page OCR and Allen 2005 Tables 1-2/1-3; the two OCRs never disagree where both are legible; about 18 cells rest on the 2005 OCR alone and rows 18-23 on Table 1-3 alone, so a maintainer should eyeball the p. 8-5 scan once; the correction targets leeway-definition rather than hf-radar-search-area.
